text:
maria: Pushed a short nsys capture from the nightly that reproduces the latency spikes. attaching heatmap & a couple of quick notes. looking for eyeballs on the flash-attn variants + kv rw hotspot.

ken: on it. which job/commit?

maria: nightly/serve-2026-03-17 commit b3f9c2 — mainly happens with batch sizes 8-16 and ctx ~2048.

alice: image link: https://internal.artifacts/heatmaps/1755554321/heat.png (hotspot at 00:02:14)

tz: quick question — is this only on A100 or repros on V100 too?

maria: repros on both but more pronounced on A100 (p99 up ~18% higher). V100 shows smaller KV write stalls.

ken: okay. did you capture the kernel names? nvtx annotation looks like the busy phase is a fused-flash variant I haven't seen before.

maria: yes — top kernels: FLASH_FWD_FUSED, KV_STORE_WRITE, FLASH_REDUCE. timeline shows KV_STORE_WRITE chaining right after the fused flash stage and blocking a following small matmul.

tracebot: nsys summary — total GPU time 12.4s, kernels counted: FLASH_FWD_FUSED (4.9s), KV_STORE_WRITE (2.7s), FLASH_REDUCE (1.3s), small_gemm (0.9s). memory copies: 0.2s.

alice: that KV_STORE_WRITE looks like the write-back path from our on-GPU kvcache. is it using the serialized write path?

maria: yes, code path: if (write_batch_size > threshold) we take slow path which does an SM-synchronized write with atomics. suspect contention.

ken: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to re-run locally with counters.

maria: sure —

```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1755 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite --cuda-memory-activity true --cuda-ptx-inst-level 2 python -m redwood.serve.benchmark --cfg nightly.json
```

ken: nice. add `--events` for instr/executed to see if bank conflicts spike. also try `--cuda-memory-activity false` to reduce overhead and increase fidelity of kernel timelines.

alice: i pulled the temp counters — there's a burst of 64B bank conflicts on SM 3 at hotspot, correlates with concurrent writes from multiple warps to contiguous KV rows.

maria: here's a short stack/context from the trace: FLASH_FWD_FUSED -> KV_STORE_WRITE [serial path] -> small_gemm -> WAIT_SYNC.

ken: hypothesis: fused flash produces output in tiled stripes and then KV writer attempts to coalesce writes but strides mismatch, causing fine-grained atomics and serialization. batching heuristics might be mixing sequences with different row alignments.

tz: do we have a repro where we force single-variant (no fuse) to compare?

maria: yes. on the same run I forced `ATTN_VARIANT=flash_no_fuse` and p99 drops ~9% but overall throughput lower. interesting: KV_STORE_WRITE time drops by 40% without fuse.

alice: that suggests the fused layout increases write amplification for kv path. maybe the fused kernel emits fragments out-of-order relative to our desired write quanta.

ken: can you upload the flattened memory offsets for a single batch? I want to see alignment.

maria: pasted offsets snippet:

```
# offsets for batch 0 (per token)
0: 0x0
1: 0x40
2: 0x80
3: 0xC0
4: 0x120  # misaligned jump here for stripe boundary
5: 0x160
...
```

ken: aha the 0xC0->0x120 jump creates a crossing of 128B boundary leading to writes split across cachelines. many warps hit atomic update path.

alice: also saw increased L2 write-back metadata in perfetto for those intervals. could be thrashing the write-combining buffers.

maria: actionable items I see: (1) test a fuse-aware KV write coalescer that groups writes by aligned 128B chunks, (2) tweak batching heuristics to avoid mixing sequences whose stripe offsets cross boundaries, (3) add an NVTX region around KV write + record per-warp active lanes.

tz: +1. also recommend kernel selection change: prefer FLASH_NO_FUSE for tail latency sensitive routes until we have coalescing. We can route by policy.

ken: I prototyped a coalescer last week. small patch: gather writes into a 128B staging buffer per CTA and flush with a single wide store. micro-benchmarks show KV_STORE_WRITE down by ~60%.

alice: do you have micro numbers?

ken: yes — synthetic bench: 1024 rows, 2048 ctx, batch=8. before: KV_WRITE 520us. after coalescer: 210us. p99 end-to-end simulated drops ~12%.

maria: can you open a PR with the patch + nvtx markers? I'll run the nightly with that coalescer toggled via env var.

ken: will do. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 (draft).

tracebot: perfetto snapshot uploaded: https://internal.perfetto/trace/1755554321/heatmap.trace

alice: one more note — batching heuristics: we currently batch purely by arrival and fill-to-target. maybe add alignment-aware batcher that tries to group tokens with same stripe offset to avoid cross-boundary mixing. low complexity change could be to compute offset%128 and prefer grouping equal remainders.

maria: good idea. that can be a quick mitigation while ken's coalescer lands.

tz: timeline: can we rollout coalescer to dedicated for a canary next week? would like to see production delta.

maria: yes — I'll schedule a canary: dedicated/canary-7 with 10% traffic and `KV_COALESCE=on` + `ATTN_VARIANT=fused` to verify we can keep fuse + coalesce.

ken: pairing note — i also found one small correctness gotcha: staging buffer needs to be zeroed for partial edge flushes or we'll leak stale bytes into KV rows. added test in PR.

alice: thanks — also recommend adding a lightweight per-request sampling metric: kv_write_frag_count so we can alert if fragmentation spikes.

maria: added to TODO list. I'll post follow-up when canary data is in (~48h). thanks everyone :) :rocket:

ken: thanks, will push CI tests and get the PR out.

alice: follow-up: if coalescer works, we can consider merged flash+kv pipeline in future to avoid host-level postprocessing. long-term item.

tracebot: note — debug capture saved to s3://redwood-traces/nightly/1755554321.tar.gz

maria: Thread summary: identified KV_STORE_WRITE hotspot caused by fused flash output alignment mis-match -> causes atomic serialization -> mitigations: add per-CTA 128B coalescer, alignment-aware batcher, fallback to no-fuse for latency-sensitive routes. will follow up with canary results.

ken: tagging @eng-sre for canary monitoring.

alice: :thumbsup:
